Streaming e-means for data that does not fit in memory

Source: R/stream.R
emeans_stream.Rd

Caller-driven training: the caller supplies rows in chunks, in any order it chooses (shuffle each epoch for best results). Each epoch must supply exactly recipe$epoch_rows[epoch] rows, grouped into batches of emeans_stream_status(s)$expected_batch rows; one batch may be split across several emeans_accumulate() calls.

Usage

emeans_stream(
  n,
  init,
  nepochs = 5,
  batch_law = c("auto", "throughput", "quality"),
  batch_size = NULL,
  alpha0 = NULL,
  spherical = FALSE,
  unused_threshold = NULL,
  precision = c("double", "single"),
  seed = 1234L,
  n_threads = NULL
)

emeans_stream_status(s)

emeans_accumulate(s, chunk)

emeans_update(s)

emeans_end_epoch(s)

emeans_finalize(s)

Arguments

n

Total number of training rows (one epoch).

init

k x d matrix of initial centers (e.g. random training rows).

nepochs

Epoch budget; fractions allowed (e.g. 1.5).

batch_law

"auto" (quality law when d <= 16, else throughput), "throughput", or "quality" (batch about 8 times smaller).

batch_size, alpha0

Optional overrides. Giving batch_size alone keeps the step law for alpha0.

spherical

Cluster unit vectors by cosine similarity. Rows of x must already be unit-norm; centers are returned as unit vectors.

unused_threshold

Revival threshold tau: clusters with mass below tau * mean(mass) are revived. NULL gives 0.1, or 0 (off) when d <= 2.

precision

"double", or "single" to store the training data and compute distances in float32 (about 2x faster, half the memory). Batch statistics, centroids and masses always accumulate in double precision, and withinss is computed from the original data. As in the faiss FP32 path, single precision assigns poorly when the data sit far from the origin (the error grows with the squared norm of the rows); centre the data first, e.g. with scale(x, scale = FALSE). Double precision hits the same limit at offsets around 1e8.

seed

Integer seed for initialization, shuffling and revival. Does not touch R's random number generator.

n_threads

Threads for assignment. Defaults to getOption("emeansR.threads"), else physical cores minus one (at most two when the _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_ environment variable is set).

s

An emeans_stream object.

chunk

Numeric matrix of rows to add to the current batch.

Value

emeans_stream() returns an emeans_stream object.

emeans_stream_status() returns a list with step, epoch (completed epochs), n_epochs, expected_batch (rows the next update needs), n_splits, and the per-epoch objective so far.

emeans_accumulate() returns the chunk's cluster labels against the centroids of the current batch (invisibly).

emeans_finalize() returns a list of class emeans_streamed with centers, obj, iteration_stats, recipe, n_splits; use predict.emeans() on it to label data.

Details

The loop is:

s <- emeans_stream(n, init, nepochs = 3)
for (epoch in seq_along(s$recipe$epoch_rows)) {
  left <- s$recipe$epoch_rows[epoch]
  while (left > 0) {
    b <- emeans_stream_status(s)$expected_batch
    emeans_accumulate(s, next_rows(b))  # next_rows(): your data reader
    emeans_update(s)
    left <- left - b
  }
  emeans_end_epoch(s)
}
fit <- emeans_finalize(s)

See the "Streaming" section of the vignette for a complete example.
